entry.evidence: There are two competing hypotheses about the formation environment of the Fe–Mn nodules: marine or terrestrial.

sequences.source_document: Published paper (PDF pp. 1-8; XML abstract and captions)

steps.action: Frame the unresolved origin of Shimajiri–Mahji soil: weathered Ryukyu limestone (terra rossa) versus weathered aeolian dust, mudstone and volcanic ash.
steps.quote: There are two hypotheses about the origins of Shimajiri–Mahji.

steps.action: Take from the literature the rival formation environments for the nodules: marine (Taira 1987; Bakker et al. 2005, on Co and Pb enrichment and U–Th growth rate) versus terrestrial soil.
steps.quote: Two formation environments have been proposed for the origin of the Fe–Mn nodules in Shimajiri–Mahji: marine and terrestrial.

steps.action: Take from published work the expected settings and traits of the nodule types (HN, DN, SSN, FWN, TN) and note that existing discrimination diagrams are inadequate.
steps.quote: there is no useful discrimination scheme today

steps.action: Design the test: bulk chemical composition plus CT and elemental imaging, to be compared with the geochemical signatures of the rival nodule types.
steps.quote: we analyzed the chemical composition and used computed tomography (CT) to clarify the origins of Fe–Mn nodules

steps.action: Use nodules collected from Shimajiri–Mahji at Yomitanson and Onnason; select five relatively large samples per site and exclude those with limestone debris.
steps.quote: Five samples of relatively large size were selected from each region. Samples accompanied by limestone debris were excluded.

steps.action: Measure the nodules by medical CT, micro-XRF Fe/Mn mapping, XRF and ICP-MS. Results: layered structures, rhythmic Mn/Fe cycles, Mn/Fe of 1.00-1.71, and strongly positive Ce and negative Y anomalies.
steps.quote: CT scanning images showed that the samples had a layered structure

steps.action: Check analytical accuracy against the reference materials JB-2 and JMS-2.
steps.quote: The analytical accuracy of the standard materials JB-2 and JMS-2 was typically within < 8 % of accepted values

steps.action: Compare compositions between the two sites; they are similar except for Ca, Ba and Pb.
steps.quote: The chemical compositions of the samples from each region were similar to each other

steps.action: Plot the samples on the Josso et al. (2017) ternary diagram with compiled literature nodules; they fall outside the HN field with TN, SSN and FWN because of low Ni and Cu.
steps.quote: the samples of this study are plotted outside the HN field together with TN, SSN, and FWN

steps.action: Exclude deep-seafloor formation (HN/DN): geochemistry, absence of a nucleus in CT, and no geologic evidence of subsidence below 800 m.
steps.quote: Therefore, the Fe–Mn nodules in Shimajiri–Mahji are unlikely to have formed on the deep seafloor.

steps.action: Compare Co, Pb and REY patterns with compiled data: Co and Pb are higher in TN than SSN, and the REY patterns match TN from Chinese terra rossa.
steps.quote: However, Co and Pb are enriched in TN rather than in SSN

steps.action: Retain terrestrial (soil) origin for the nodules.
steps.quote: we concluded that the Fe–Mn nodules in Shimajiri–Mahji are terrestrial in origin

steps.action: Adopt from published work the expectation that low Mn/Fe layers mark reducing (wet) soil and high Mn/Fe layers mark oxidizing (dry) soil.
steps.quote: a layer with a lower Mn/Fe ratio should indicate relatively reducing soil conditions

steps.action: Convert the Mn/Fe cycle spacing (0.34-0.37 mm/cycle) to time using the cited 61 mm/Myr growth rate, giving 5.5-6.1 kyr per cycle.
steps.quote: high or low Mn/Fe layers formed repeatedly at 5.5–6.1 kyr/cycle

steps.action: Compare the inferred cycle with millennial East Asian monsoon periodicities from Wang et al. (2008).
steps.quote: [...] mostly consists with the changes in temporal intensity of the East Asian monsoon

steps.action: Retain the interpretation that the Mn/Fe layering records soil-moisture changes tied to monsoon intensity.
steps.quote: the layered pattern of Mn/Fe ratios probably reflects changes in the soil moisture

steps.action: Infer from CT dense and sparse layers (after Yu et al. 2020) up to three gradual and two rapid drying periods, and estimate ages of about 0 and 80 ka from the assumed growth rate.
steps.quote: the samples would have experienced up to three periods of a gradual increase in redox potential

steps.action: Compare the inferred dense-layer timing with warm periods in the Vostok δ18O record.
steps.quote: These estimated ages are consistent with our interpretation that the alternating layers of variable density can be associated with climate change

steps.action: Pose the need for a discrimination scheme that separates SSN from FWN as well as the other nodule types.
steps.quote: cannot discriminate between SSN and FWN

steps.action: Compile literature compositions of TN, FWN, SSN, HN and DN and compare element abundances in box plots.
steps.quote: We compared the elemental abundances of TN, FWN, SSN, HN, and DN by using box plots

steps.action: Compare published growth rates of the nodule types with their Co abundance order to justify Co/Rb as a discriminant.
steps.quote: This mostly coincides with the order of Co abundance.

steps.action: Construct an Al/Na versus Co/Rb discrimination diagram with fields for terrestrial soil, lakes, shallow seas and deep ocean, noting slight FWN–SSN overlap.
steps.quote: The new discrimination diagram based on Al/Na and Co/Rb ratios (Fig. 7) can classify-four formation [...]

steps.action: Plot the study samples on the new diagram; they fall in the terrestrial field, consistent with the earlier comparisons.
steps.quote: the samples from this study were plotted in the terrestrial field

steps.action: Exclude shallow-sea and lake origins on Co, Pb and Ce anomaly evidence.
steps.quote: the high Co and Pb contents and positive Ce anomaly of the nodules are not consistent with SSN and FWN

steps.action: Retain terrestrial nodule origin and extend it to the soil question: Shimajiri–Mahji originated from weathered Ryukyu limestone.
steps.quote: strongly indicating that Shimajiri–Mahji originated from weathered Ryukyu limestone

steps.action: Replace Fig. 4 so the comparison bands match the caption (FWN from Lake Baikal instead of the deep-submarine western North Pacific nodules plotted originally) and revise the caption.

end.claim: The Fe–Mn nodules of Shimajiri–Mahji formed in terrestrial soil, like terra rossa nodules, rather than in the deep ocean, shallow seas or lakes, indicating that the soil derives from weathered Ryukyu limestone.

decisive_move.sentence: Comparing the nodules' Ni+Cu, Co, Pb and REY signatures with compiled literature data for each nodule type (Figs. 4-6) is what places them with terrestrial nodules and excludes the marine rivals.

gates.evidence: The marine-vs-terrestrial rivals motivated the choice of geochemical analyses (p. 2), but the samples were offered by another researcher (Acknowledgements, p. 7), not collected for the test. The samples could have plotted in the HN/DN or SSN fields (p. 4), but the shallow-sea exclusion rests on qualitative Co/Pb and Ce comparisons. The new diagram's fields were drawn after the data were compiled, so applying it to the study samples is not an independent test. Nothing was fixed in advance.

imports.item: Medical X-ray CT scanner (Canon Aquilion PRIME/Focus Edition) used to image nodule internal density

novelty_claims.quote: A new discrimination diagram based on Al/Na and Co/Rb ratios was developed for classifying the formation environments of Fe–Mn nodules
Therefore, we suggest a new discrimination diagram of Fe–Mn nodules based [...] .

limits: The XML text supplied contains only the abstract and captions, so body steps are located by printed page. Sub-claims at other statuses: (a) Mn/Fe layering records millennial East Asian monsoon variation, best_explanation at most, stated as 'probably' (p. 5); (b) CT density layers record warm periods at <10, 40-50 and ~80 ka, a weak best_explanation resting on an assumed growth rate (p. 5); (c) the Al/Na–Co/Rb diagram, capability_characterized only partly: fields drawn on the compiled literature data with no held-out validation and an acknowledged FWN–SSN overlap (p. 6); (d) the soil origin from weathered limestone is inferred from the nodule origin and is not tested directly (p. 6). The time conversion uses one 1979 U–Th growth rate (61 ± 9 mm/Myr) with no propagated uncertainty and no dating of the study samples. Only ten nodules were analysed and two mapped; the paper does not report how the two mapped nodules were chosen. Inference: rejecting deep-ocean formation partly relies on the absence of reported subsidence evidence rather than a measurement. No peer-review file was supplied. A corrigendum (PDF p. 10) shows that the published Fig. 4 originally plotted deep-submarine nodules where the caption named FWN, so the REY comparison as first printed did not match its text. The data-availability statements conflict: one says the data are in the paper and supplement, the other says data are available on request. Box plots and Fig. A1 are in a supplement not supplied.

disagreements.target: Taira (1987) and Bakker et al. (2005): nodules grew on the seafloor because of high Co and Pb
disagreements.support: Compiled data show Co and Pb are enriched in terrestrial nodules rather than shallow-sea nodules, and the REY patterns match terra rossa nodules.
disagreements.quote: However, Co and Pb are enriched in TN rather than in SSN

disagreements.target: Inoue and Mizota (1988), Tokashiki (1993), Tokashiki et al. (1991): Shimajiri–Mahji derives from aeolian dust, mudstone and volcanic ash
disagreements.support: Terrestrial (terra rossa-like) nodule origin is taken to indicate a weathered-limestone soil; aeolian and volcanic minerals also occur in terra rossa.
disagreements.quote: However, minerals originating from Aeolian dust, volcanic ash, and mudstone are commonly found in terra rossa

disagreements.target: Nicholson (1992) geochemical discrimination diagrams of nodule origins
disagreements.support: Cited as shown incomplete by later published data; no test performed here.
disagreements.quote: the geochemical discrimination diagrams have been revealed to be incomplete with increase of published geochemical data

disagreements.target: Ternary and REY discrimination scheme (Josso et al., 2017, Fig. 5)
disagreements.support: On compiled data the scheme separates oceanic types but not shallow-sea from freshwater nodules, motivating the new diagram.
disagreements.quote: cannot discriminate between SSN and FWN
